publications.audience: the owner of a mechanical contracting business

issues.headline: HVAC manufacturers moved October 9 to dismiss price-fixing class actions alleging they coordinated equipment increases since January 2020, including a class of commercial indirect purchasers.
issues.summary: HVAC manufacturers moved October 9 to dismiss price-fixing class actions over equipment increases since 2020; HARDI distributor sales rose 7.6 percent in August, IAPMO published its Water Demand Calculator as an American National Standard, H.R. 10851 became the first national plug-in solar bill, and a typical supermarket refrigeration system leaks about 25 percent of its charge a year — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: AHRI's August central air conditioner shipments rose 17.2% to 418,323 units, but gas furnaces fell 4.3% and combined air conditioner and heat pump shipments sank 26% from June.
issues.summary: AHRI's August central air conditioner shipments rose 17.2 percent to 418,323 while gas furnaces fell 4.3 percent; California's SB 690 ends private website pen-register suits from January 1, controls and air-distribution makers posted October price increases, Watsco closed its Granite Group purchase, and EPA published its 2027 HFC allowance notice — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: NFPA's code panel deadlocked 10-10 on a two-year delay, so the September 1 GFCI requirement for outdoor HVAC equipment stands while ACCA and AHRI appeal.
issues.summary: NFPA's code panel deadlocked 10-10 on delaying the outdoor HVAC GFCI requirement, which took effect September 1 while ACCA appeals; the construction materials price index has risen every month since April, Section 301 forced-labor duties of 10 or 12.5 percent now reach 60 economies, Commerce set 82.03 to 153.67 percent duties on Laotian solar cells, and a judge vacated EPA's termination of the $7 billion Solar for All program — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: Canada's retaliatory tariffs on roughly $27.6 billion of U.S. goods took effect September 8, and Washington modifies its own 50% Section 338 duty list on September 15.
issues.summary: Canada's retaliatory tariffs hit $27.6 billion of U.S. goods on September 8 and Washington modifies its own 50% Section 338 list on September 15; five HVAC makers posted 5–15% September increases, CBP starts rejecting copper entries that do not declare a smelt country on September 14, Commerce set 147–268% duties on solar cells from three countries, and supermarket refrigeration faces a 1,400 GWP ceiling from January 1 — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: The IRS confirmed on August 10 that employers must report FLSA overtime premiums in box 12 of the 2026 Form W-2 under a new code TT
issues.summary: The IRS made 2026 overtime a W-2 reporting problem, Commerce proposed tariffing heat exchanger parts and electric cable, an August 26 executive order shut foreign transformers and inverters out of the bulk power grid, solar modules got a $0.38-a-watt price floor, and June equipment shipments jumped — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: Section 232 tariffs cut residential HVAC duty to 15%, but commercial refrigeration, copper pipe and electrical wire still pay 25% as copper hit a record $6.71 a pound
issues.summary: Plumbing and HVAC/R distributors posted August 2026 price hikes from 3% to 25%, the EV charger tax credit expired June 30, lead-service-line replacement plans are due November 1, 2027, and Texas adopts the 2026 electrical code September 1 — every claim sourced.

publications.audience: the owner of a building, roofing or renovation business

issues.headline: Florida insurers had logged 46,509 Isaias claims and about $582 million of insured damage by October 15, with 87% of residential claims still open and unpaid.
issues.summary: Florida insurers logged 46,509 Isaias claims and about $582 million of insured damage by October 15; Verisk adds a material handling line to its November 1 Xactimate price lists, September housing completions fell 14.0 percent from a year earlier, GAF stopped selling WeatherSide fiber-cement siding, and builder sentiment fell to 29 — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: Hurricane Isaias hit Destin, Florida, as a Category 2 on October 9, and Cotality puts insured wind and surge losses at $2 billion to $3 billion.
issues.summary: Hurricane Isaias hit Destin, Florida, as a Category 2 on October 9 with Cotality putting insured losses at $2 billion to $3 billion; Florida's price-gouging law names roof repair and tree removal, NAHB's remodeling index rose to 62, and exterior and trim makers announced increases of 3 to 10 percent — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: August housing completions fell to a 1,128,000 annual rate, 27.1 percent below a year earlier, while single-family starts rose 7.6 percent and builders deepened price cuts.
issues.summary: August housing completions fell to a 1,128,000 annual rate while 38 percent of builders cut prices; the 30-year mortgage averaged 7.03 percent, hot-rolled coil is $1,220 a ton, fall protection again led OSHA's most-cited list with 4,041 citations, no Atlantic hurricane had formed by September 21, and Florida's 9th Edition code takes effect December 31 — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: Construction unemployment hit a record-low 3.1 percent in August even as 87 percent of firms reported unfilled craft openings and 42 percent blamed shortages for project delays.
issues.summary: Construction unemployment hit a record-low 3.1 percent in August with 87 percent of firms carrying unfilled craft jobs; steel mill products are up 23.4 percent and copper wire 27.2 percent over the year, FinCEN permanently exempted U.S. firms from beneficial ownership reporting, private residential spending fell to an $859.0 billion rate, and the 30-year fixed rose a third straight week to 6.76 percent — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: New-home demand broke in July: housing starts fell 12.4 percent, new-home sales fell 10.5 percent, and unsold new houses reached 9.6 months of supply
issues.summary: July housing starts fell 12.4 percent and new-home sales 10.5 percent while construction input costs ran 7.1 percent above a year ago; Cal/OSHA split $282,420 across three roofers on one job site; the 2027 IECC went final; and the whole steel-framing shelf reprices September 1.

issues.headline: A 50% tariff on Canadian cement, plywood and furniture takes effect August 19 under a century-old trade law, even as softwood lumber duties keep falling
issues.summary: OSHA proposed a $172,324 roofing-fall fine, California's contractor workers'-comp fines doubled to $10,000-$20,000, Sherwin-Williams raised paint 9% and bulk solvent 18% on May 1, and impact windows now cost $1,200 to $2,250 more per project — every claim sourced.

publications.audience: the owner of a residential services business

issues.headline: Rollins grew residential pest revenue only 2.3% organically in the third quarter, and operating margin fell 140 basis points to 20.5% as customer acquisition stayed under pressure.
issues.summary: Rollins grew residential pest revenue only 2.3 percent organically in the third quarter as margin fell 140 basis points; Pool Corporation's sales rose 4 percent with gross margin down to 29.0 percent, CPSC warned on PowRyte pressure washers and Kalorik air fryer ovens, and truck freight producer prices were up 19.3 percent over the year — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: Leslie's, the largest pool supply chain with more than 900 stores, filed Chapter 11 on September 30 to erase $685 million of debt, a day after closing about 76 stores.
issues.summary: Leslie's, the largest pool supply chain, filed Chapter 11 on September 30 to erase $685 million of debt; DR Power recalled about 42,860 trimmer mowers after 19 fires, PHTA opened applications to revise the aboveground pool standard, FMCSA lengthened emergency hours-of-service relief to 30 days, and repair and maintenance producer prices rose 7.3 percent in a year — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: Commercial auto rates rose 3.58% and general liability 4.18% in August while workers' comp fell 1.1%, and WTW put overall second-quarter commercial pricing up just 0.5%.
issues.summary: Commercial auto insurance rates rose 3.58 percent and general liability 4.18 percent in August while workers' comp fell 1.1 percent; EPA closed registration review on 20 canceled pesticide cases, the waters-of-the-U.S. proposal opens comment to October 9, the 33,000-visa H-2B cap filled September 4, Commerce set a 56.43 percent preliminary margin on Mexican copper tube, and PHTA published the 2026 public pool standard — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: Wholesale diesel jumped 24.1% in August alone and is up 77.8% over the year, BLS reported September 10, with truck freight producer prices up 14.3%.
issues.summary: Wholesale diesel jumped 24.1 percent in August and 77.8 percent over the year while truck freight producer prices rose 14.3 percent; EPA's applicator-certification clearance lapsed August 31 with comments closing September 28, CPSC warned on pressure washers without GFCI plugs and non-compliant pool drain covers, and FMCSA pulled 110 CDL schools and 28,000 drivers in an August 31 crackdown — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: Pending home sales fell 2.3% in July to 71.2, the lowest since January, and new single-family sales fell 10.5% to a 607,000 annual rate
issues.summary: Pending home sales fell to 71.2 and new single-family sales to a 607,000 annual rate, fewer than 3,000 H-2B numbers remain in the first-half FY2027 cap, DOE's commercial water heater standard binds October 6, and diesel hit $5.652 a gallon - every claim sourced.

issues.headline: BLS's July CPI shows motor fuel up 24.8% over the year while motor vehicle insurance fell 4.5%, its second straight monthly decline, released August 12, 2026
issues.summary: Water, sewer and trash prices rose 4.6% against 3.4% overall CPI, the H-2B supplemental window stays open until September 15, PoolCorp's Q2 sales hit $1.8 billion as margin slipped to 29.7%, and Commerce proposed 25% tariffs on cargo trailers — every claim sourced.

publications.audience: the owner of a commercial services or facilities business

issues.headline: Massachusetts' fire prevention board voted to require annual checks for recalled sprinkler heads, with property owners responsible for notifying the fire department and replacing them.
issues.summary: Massachusetts' fire prevention board voted to require annual checks for recalled sprinkler heads; OSHA's revised Hazard Communication Standard is scheduled to take effect by November 20, more than 100 groups backed the Senate's permitting bill, Schindler's Americas modernization orders fell more than 10 percent, and USDA proposed easing its beef maturation rule — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: Building service contractors expect wage demands to rise, 72.5% say, and 82.3% expect higher supply and operating costs, while 32% plan robotic floor equipment within 12 months, about double 2025.
issues.summary: Building service contractors expect wage demands to rise (72.5 percent) and supply and operating costs to rise (82.3 percent), with 32 percent planning robotic floor equipment; Cintas and UniFirst agreed not to close before December 11, NFSA said steel and CPVC can be mixed in one sprinkler system, and Maryland banned dynamic pricing by food retailers — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: Cintas lifted its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook to $12.15-$12.27 billion on September 23 and expects its FTC-reviewed UniFirst purchase to close before the end of 2026.
issues.summary: Cintas raised its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook to $12.15-12.27 billion and expects its UniFirst purchase to close by year-end; NFPA 25's 2026 edition makes a frozen sprinkler system an impairment, the stopgap funds surface transportation only to December 11, OSHA's heat rule slipped to a December proposal, and the FCC Covered List has grown three times in nine months — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: On-highway diesel hit $5.967 a gallon on September 7, up 36.8 cents in a week and $2.20 from a year ago, with wholesale diesel up 24.1% in August.
issues.summary: On-highway diesel hit $5.967 a gallon on September 7, up $2.20 in a year; construction inputs rose about 8.9 percent with steel mill products up 23.4 percent, Maryland's posted asphalt reached $807.50 a ton, the H-2B first-half FY2027 cap filled on September 4, and New York's elevator rule adds an $815 per-device pre-inspection fee — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: A 50% additional duty on 554 lines of Canadian goods — cement, plastics, adhesives, machinery, electrical equipment and carpet among them — took effect August 22
issues.summary: A 50% Section 338 duty on 554 lines of Canadian goods took effect August 22, Missouri's asphalt index moved again to $631.25, diesel hit $5.652 a gallon, the SCA fringe rate rose to $5.92, and commercial property premiums fell 6.3% — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: Construction input prices were flat in July 2026 but 7.4% above a year ago, with steel mill products up 22.5% and diesel up over 50 cents a gallon
issues.summary: Missouri's posted asphalt price jumped 24.4% to $605.00 by June, the construction backlog indicator fell to 8.0 months, commercial property insurance fell 8.1% for a fifth straight quarter, and NFPA 72 cuts the alarm-impairment window from 24 hours to 8 — every claim sourced.

publications.audience: the owner of a professional services firm

issues.headline: HHS handed CMS power to exclude providers from federal health programs in a notice published October 14, effective immediately, with no hearing authority and, attorneys say, no stated criteria for when it will use it.
issues.summary: HHS gave CMS power to exclude providers from federal health programs in a notice effective October 14; Baltimore sued Yardi over hidden rent-payment fees, TIGTA tied potential ghost preparers to about $179 million in refund claims, the 2027 Social Security wage base is $192,300, and OneKey became the third MLS to reject Compass — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: California Regional MLS sued Compass on October 5 to defend its listing rules, a day before Compass's deadline to stop fining agents who publicly market office exclusives.
issues.summary: California Regional MLS sued Compass on October 5 over its listing rules; HUD's NSPIRE scoring began counting new deficiencies October 1, the Senate passed the Taxpayer Assistance and Service Act and a Terrorism Risk Insurance reauthorization, Connecticut's SB 340 took effect, and temp help employment fell 10,900 in September — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: The SBA extended comment on its plan to replace nearly 1,000 small-business size standards with 338 by 60 days, moving the deadline to November 20
issues.summary: The SBA extended comment on its size-standards overhaul to November 20; three Maryland housing laws take effect October 1, IRS Notice 2026-60 sets per diem at $329 and $230, the estate tax closing letter fee rises to $76, CMS canceled about 315,000 marketplace enrollments, and flood insurance authority expires December 11 — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: The stopgap the House cleared 370-48 on September 1 extends National Flood Insurance Program authority only through December 11, the 36th short-term flood reauthorization since 2017
issues.summary: The September 1 stopgap extends National Flood Insurance authority only to December 11 — the 36th short-term reauthorization since 2017; HUD's FY2027 Fair Market Rents take effect October 1, the Medicare conversion factor falls to $33.17, California's FAIR Plan cuts producer commissions on October 15, Aon is buying USI for $17 billion, and existing-home sales fell to a 3.98 million rate — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: The SBA proposed on August 20 to cut nearly 1,000 small-business size standards down to 338, making 114,541 more firms eligible for federal contracts and SBA loans
issues.summary: SBA would cut nearly 1,000 size standards to 338, DHS proposes a $103,265 H-1B fee, the EO 11246 contractor rules die October 26, FIRE shuts off November 19, and Do Not Call access hits $85 an area code.

issues.headline: FinCEN's August 14 final rule permanently ends federal beneficial-ownership reporting for domestic small businesses, exempting an estimated 32 million companies from Corporate Transparency Act filings
issues.summary: RentGrow will pay $2.25 million to settle FTC tenant-screening claims, the No Surprises Act arbitration fee drops from $115 to $15, the IRS mileage rate rises to 76 cents July 1, and the blocked $100,000 H-1B fee expires September 20 — every claim sourced.

publications.audience: the owner of an independent practice

issues.headline: Wedgewood Pharmacy recalled nearly 4,000 compounded veterinary product listings on October 21 over potency doubts, covering shipments from February 18 to October 6 that reached practices nationwide.
issues.summary: Wedgewood Pharmacy recalled nearly 4,000 compounded veterinary product listings on October 21; HHS gave $51 million to 28 health centers for children's dental care, FDA classified a compounded tirzepatide recall Class II, FDA warned on counterfeit Ocusan eye drops, and DOJ charged a $1.62 billion addiction-treatment billing scheme — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: Nearly two in five dentists say they are not busy enough in the third quarter, up from about one in four in Q2, while reimbursement gains trail inflation.
issues.summary: Nearly two in five dentists say they are not busy enough in the third quarter, up from about one in four in Q2; flumazenil is on back order, the ADA asked Senate Finance to extend insurance reform to stand-alone dental plans, AVMA put average veterinary practice revenue at $1.57 million, and CDC reported botulism-type cases from unapproved toxin — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: The Fed raised rates a quarter point to 3.75-4.00% on September 16 and banks lifted prime to 7.00% the next day, repricing every practice loan tied to it.
issues.summary: The Fed raised rates to 3.75-4.00 percent on September 16 and prime went to 7.00 percent; veterinary prices rose 5.7 percent in the year to August, the ADA told a House panel the three largest dental insurers hold 38 to 97 percent of a state's group market, and the Labor Department narrowed its parity enforcement to three areas — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: Dental prices rose 5.0% and veterinary 5.7% in the year to August while physicians' services rose 2.0% and eye care 1.3%, Labor Department data released September 11 show
issues.summary: Dental prices rose 5.0 percent and veterinary 5.7 percent in the year to August against 2.0 percent for physicians' services; CMS told states to restrict dental amalgam coverage, 85 percent of veterinary clients balk at $1,000 estimates, Ohio fined a med spa $25,000 and added quarterly medical-director inspections, and the DEA's telemedicine rule reached OIRA against a December 31 cliff — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: Treasury made the Corporate Transparency Act exemption permanent on August 11 and the rule took effect August 14, ending beneficial ownership filing for U.S.-formed practices
issues.summary: Treasury made the Corporate Transparency Act exemption permanent August 14, ending beneficial ownership filing for U.S.-formed practices; small-group health premiums are filed up a median 14% for 2027; CDT 2027 changes 67 dental codes; South Carolina bars research-grade peptides; Medicaid renewals are backing up before work reporting starts.

issues.headline: CMS proposed cutting the Medicare conversion factor 1.68% to $32.84 for 2027, adding a richer visit-complexity modifier and new remote-monitoring staffing rules; comments close September 14
issues.summary: Dental staff costs are up 23% since 2021 while insurance reimbursement rose 21% and Medicaid 18%, Medicaid work requirements begin October 1, Indiana's first med-spa law requires registration by January 1, 2027, and HHS awarded $223.1 million in behavioral-health grants — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: Washington's rewritten claims rules took effect October 18: insurers have five business days to answer a shop's supplement in writing, and total-loss comparable searches stop at 150 miles.
issues.summary: Washington's rewritten claims rules took effect October 18, giving insurers five business days to answer a shop's supplement; CCC agreed to a $7.75-a-share take-private, FCA US recalled 265,512 Ram ProMaster vans, Michelin's replacement tire volume rose 4 percent, and Rinsed reported same-store retail car-wash revenue down 9.6 percent — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: California chaptered SB 988 on September 27, making windshield shops disclose driver-assistance calibration needs and report results in writing, with civil penalties up to $2,000 per repeat violation.
issues.summary: California chaptered SB 988 on September 27, requiring windshield shops to disclose and report driver-assistance calibration; insurers pay total-loss administrative fees 75 percent of the time, total losses hit a record 23.1 percent of claims, NHTSA opened a lighting-standard rulemaking, and Americans drove 28.6 miles a day in 2025 — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: eBay's ban on airbags, inflators and steering-wheel airbag covers took effect September 24, closing the largest marketplace for the parts and giving sellers 30 days to clear listings.
issues.summary: eBay's ban on airbags, inflators and steering-wheel airbag covers took effect September 24; franchised dealers ran body shops at 31.9 percent of stores, Ford filed six recalls led by about 223,500 F-150s, the Steelworkers asked for a Section 201 tire case, and unlimited wash member price satisfaction fell to 46 percent — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: Pump prices jumped 13 cents in a week to a $4.277 national average and diesel reached $6.204 a gallon as crude climbed back toward $100 a barrel.
issues.summary: Pump prices jumped 13 cents in a week to a $4.277 average and diesel reached $6.204 a gallon; a federal jury hit Progressive with $40 million in Oklahoma, eBay bans all airbag listings from September 24 after an eleventh inflator death, USTMA cut its 2026 tire forecast below 2025, Louisiana's towing act took effect August 1, and a Colorado car wash paid $1.35 million over cancellation practices — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: Washington's insurance commissioner signed a claims-handling rule on Aug. 18 that from Oct. 18 gives insurers five business days to answer a shop's supplement in writing
issues.summary: Washington's claims-handling rule takes effect Oct. 18, Texas insurers must comply with mandatory appraisal from Sept. 1, and CPI shows vehicle repair prices up 6.6% while auto insurance prices fell 4.5% — every claim sourced.

issues.headline: TechForce's 2026 report finds U.S. auto-service, collision and diesel shops face a combined 43,135-technician annual shortfall, with collision hiring covering only 43 percent of need
issues.summary: Commerce set a final tire-tariff rate up to 78.33% on August 14, Illinois' right-to-appraisal law takes effect July 1, 2027, and Mister Car Wash went private at roughly $3.1 billion as ZIPS filed Chapter 11 with $653.9 million in debt — every claim sourced.
